Sign-of-Life — memory optimisation step

Alif RTSS-HE (revB, GCC) · QVGA 320×240 · cases: busStation, canoe · 2026-08-03

What this covers. Two changes that together took the Sign-of-Life stage from does not link to links with margin: the HSV shadow filter is now off by default, and connected components was rewritten from flood fill to two-pass union-find. Every figure below is measured, either from the linker map or from the host reference pipeline — none are estimates.

1. Why the optimisation was needed

The pipeline needs about a megabyte of working memory per QVGA frame, and none of it can come from the heap: the system heap is 172 KiB in DTCM, and the sensing thread's stack is 12 KiB against a 230,400 B denoised frame. So the storage is two statically reserved .bss arenas, sized at compile time and placed by explicit linker section:

  • Persistent (.bss.sol_persistent → SRAM0) — background model state, allocated once and never reset.
  • Scratch (.bss.sol_scratch → SRAM1) — everything with a single-frame lifetime, reset at the top of every Process().

Because both are static arrays, only a reduction in the worst case frees any SRAM. Lowering the typical peak improves telemetry and nothing else. That constraint is what made the two changes below algorithmic rather than a matter of tuning.

1.1 The shortfall

Before this step the arenas simply did not fit. Both figures matched the linker to the byte, so the diagnosis was never in doubt — the arenas were larger than the free space:

On the persistent side the split was starker: of 1,536,000 B, the background model's mean and variance planes took 614,400 B and the shadow filter's RGB reference took 921,600 B — 60 % of the persistent arena, and on its own more than the entire SRAM0 headroom. Those two facts set the agenda: attack the shadow reference and connected components.

2. Change 1 — shadow filtration off by default

The HSV veto removes cast-shadow pixels: a shadowed surface keeps its hue and saturation while its brightness drops by a bounded factor, so a foreground pixel is vetoed when all three of valueRatio ∈ [0.40, 0.95], |Δsaturation| ≤ 40 and circular |Δhue| ≤ 12 hold against the background reference.

The HSV itself costs nothing — it is computed per pixel inside the loop, and only for pixels that are still foreground, so no HSV image is ever materialised. The veto's entire footprint is the exponentially-weighted RGB reference it compares against: float × w·h × 3 = 921,600 B of persistent arena.

All three HSV channels are required if the veto is kept — a value-only test vetoes anything merely darker than its background, which deletes real objects. Measured on the host reference, dropping the hue and saturation conditions collapses the canoe F-measure from 0.92 to 0.19. The question was therefore not "can it be made smaller" but "is it earning 921,600 B".

The decision itself does not change

CaseFramesSign-of-Life, veto on Sign-of-Life, veto offPer-frame flags identical?
canoe511yes

Across all 11 frames the Sign-of-Life flag is identical with and without the veto. The reason is the area gate: on canoe frame 241 the veto-off run reports 13 objects, but the largest is 392 px — every one of them sits above the 150 px minArea floor and below the 500 px areaThreshold trigger, so none of them ever reached the output signal.

What is genuinely lost. The veto does suppress sub-threshold clutter: canoe frame 241 goes from 1 reported object to 13, and frame 481 from 0 to 4. The flag is unchanged, but the object list is noisier on high-texture frames. A consumer that reads blobs rather than signOfLife would see the difference. That is the trade being made for 921,600 B.

2.2 The switch

The veto had to become a build-time switch, not just a runtime one: the persistent arena is a statically sized .bss array, so a runtime flag alone would leave the array at full size and free nothing.

SettingPersistent arenavs free SRAM0 (1,144,304)
SOL_SHADOW_VETO=OFF (default)614,656fits — 529,648 B margin
SOL_SHADOW_VETO=ON1,536,256391,952 B over — does not link

build.sh --shadow-veto / --no-shadow-veto drive the CMake option, which drives both the arena sizing and the default of the runtime PipelineConfig::shadowEnabled. Runtime may switch the veto off further but never on beyond what the build budgeted — SignOfLifeDetector::Init() rejects that combination with a diagnostic rather than overrunning the arena. Today --shadow-veto is usable on the native/host build, which is where its effect on detection quality should be evaluated; making it usable on target needs the reference quantised to uint16 Q8.8 (460,800 B) or a resolution change.

3. Change 2 — new blob-search method

Connected components was 39.3 % of the scratch peak, and most of that was one buffer. The old implementation was an iterative flood fill with an explicit stack of pixel indices, reserved to the full frame because a single component can in principle cover it: uint32 × 76,800 = 307,200 B, purely worst-case insurance.

3.1 Two-pass union-find (Rosenfeld & Pfaltz; He et al.)

The replacement is the textbook algorithm — the same family OpenCV's connectedComponentsWithStats uses:

  1. Pass 1 raster-scans once. Each foreground pixel takes the smallest label among the neighbours the scan has already visited (north-west, north, north-east and west for 8-connectivity; north and west for 4-), or a fresh provisional label. Equivalences discovered along the way go into a union-find table with path compression.
  2. Pass 2 flattens the table, renumbers the roots, resolves the label image and accumulates the per-blob bounding box, area and centroid.

Because it only ever looks backwards, it needs no pixel stack at all. Two details carry the implementation and are easy to lose in a refactor:

  • The union step always points the larger root at the smaller, so parent[l] ≤ l holds for every label. That is what lets a single ascending sweep both flatten the table and renumber the roots in place. A separate root→final map is the obvious way to write it, and it does not fit: at the worst case it is a second content-sized array that pushes the budget 7,117 B past the free region.
  • Ascending root order is exactly raster order of first appearance — a component's root is the smallest provisional label in it, which is the one created at its topmost-leftmost pixel. So component numbering matches the flood fill it replaced with no first-seen bookkeeping, which is what preserves bit-parity.

3.2 Cost

BufferFlood fillTwo-pass union-find
Label image (uint16 × w·h)153,600153,600
Flood-fill stack (uint32 × w·h)307,2000
Union-find table (uint16 × 38,401)—76,802
Per-component accumulators (capped at 4,096)—36,864
Total460,800267,266

193,534 B saved, and every term is reserved to a bound rather than sized from the frame — so the peak stays content-independent, which is the property the arena sizing depends on. Verified: the scratch peak is byte-identical (977,666) across checkerboard, isolated-pixel, flat, rectangle and noise frames.

The same two passes are implemented in all three code bases — the Python reference, the host C++ port and the Alif tree — so they remain interchangeable as references for one another.

4. The Alif / C++ implementation

4.1 Memory model

The algorithm bodies are ordinary C++ using std::vector; what differs is where the bytes come from. SolArena.hpp defines a stateless allocator that bump-allocates from one of two arenas selected by a tag type:

template <typename T> using ScratchVector    = std::vector<T, ArenaAllocator<T, ScratchArenaTag>>;
template <typename T> using PersistentVector = std::vector<T, ArenaAllocator<T, PersistentArenaTag>>;

So labels, the union-find table, the model planes and the frame buffers move, resize and return by value exactly as before, but malloc is never called. That is what let the algorithm bodies be ported unchanged and verified bit-identical against the host reference.

The allocator is LIFO: a block is reclaimed only if it sits at the top of the arena. That detail is load-bearing, and it bit during this work — the union-find table was originally allocated before the per-component accumulators, and the accumulators' 4-byte alignment left the table's 76,802 B stranded on return, inflating the peak by 39,936 B. Declaring the accumulators first, so the table is allocated last and given back first, recovered it.

4.2 Placement

Both arenas carry an explicit linker section rather than falling into the *(.bss.*) catch-all. This matters across subsystems: RTSS-HE routes .bss to SRAM0, but RTSS-HP routes it to a 1 MB DTCM, where a multi-megabyte array would silently overflow the region. With explicit sections a subsystem that has not declared them fails at link with an orphan-section placement error instead of mis-locating a buffer.

The image links. Measured scratch peak is 977,666 B, 94.8 % of its arena, down from 1,171,200 B.

SRAM1 has ~44 KB of headroom. Any new static in that region — or any full-frame temporary added to Pipeline::Process() — will break the link. Re-measure before and after such a change; SignOfLifeDetector::Process() warns once if the observed peak eats into the 32 KiB slack, so drift shows up in the log rather than as a failure much later.

Sign-of-Life outputidentical on all 11 reference frames—
  • Connected components cost 193,534 B and cost nothing in behaviour — verified bit-identical, including label numbering, in all three implementations.
  • The shadow veto cost 921,600 B and, on this data, bought no change in the Sign-of-Life decision and a slightly worse F-measure on busStation. It is off by default and kept behind a build flag rather than deleted, so it can be re-evaluated on real deployment data.
Still research. This step made the stage fit and links the image; it did not make the detector correct for the target use case. Two open items sit above it: the area thresholds (minArea = 150, areaThreshold = 500) are inherited from the busStation people-detection reference and are wrong for abandoned-object detection in an office scene, and the background-model lifetime across STOP-mode reboots is unresolved. The veto measurements here are two sequences and 11 frames — indicative of the effect, not a benchmark, and neither sequence is the target scene.
